draft.caption: Hey gays! Galing Cubao Expo? Para sa mga beks ang candle na 'to, kasi alam naming may taste kayo at aesthetic ang mga kwarto niyo. Elle's Candles, Ilang-ilang, ₱350 per jar. Message us!

reasons.note: Calls the reader gay. Meta doesn't allow ads that say or imply a viewer's sexuality, even as a friendly greeting. Talk about the scent and the shelf, not about who is reading.
Says the candle is for gay men because they have taste. That's a cliché, and it shuts out everyone else who thrifts. Keep the cheek and aim it at the ilang-ilang.
reasons.rule: No 'this is for a type of person'

Promises better sleep and tells people to light it as they fall asleep. That's a claim and it's unsafe. Say 'patayin bago matulog' instead.
reasons.rule: Sleep claim and an unsafe tip
reasons.quote: Sindihan pagkauwi para makatulog ka agad.

cuts.reason: Anyone could like candles, so there is no one moment to write a post for.
A label about age and gender, not a buying moment. The hosting moment it points at is already kept as 'Noche Buena hosts', which anyone can be in.
Same moment as 'Condo folks on a Saturday reset': making a small rented place feel like yours. The Saturday reset is more specific.
A label about age and mental state, not a buying moment, and reaching it would need stress-relief claims Elle doesn't make.
Same place and crowd as 'Roommates splitting the bills'. The shared unit has the clearer reason to buy, and gaming fits inside that post.
A candle can't be lit in a moving car, and soy wax softens in a car parked in the sun. For this crowd the candle makes sense at the unit, which is kept.
Same moment as 'Officemates buying an exchange gift': a Christmas gift for someone. The office draw has a budget and a date, so that one stays.
Soy wax can soften and glass can crack after weeks in a hot cargo container, and Elle hasn't said how she packs for shipping.
Giveaways need dozens of jars by a fixed date. Small home batches at ₱350 don't fit, and Elle hasn't set a bulk price.
Elle sells on Shopee, Instagram and Facebook, not TikTok, and this group is defined by an app, not by a moment.
Elle doesn't sell in stores, so people browsing a mall shelf can't buy where they are looking.
Every home wants to smell nice, so this says nothing about when someone would buy.

icp.headline: Your people: Noche Buena hosts.
icp.who: Someone who has guests over this December and gets the sala ready before they arrive. Thirty minutes before the doorbell: the guest glasses are out, but the house still smells like lunch.
icp.reachedMostly: Mostly women, largest group 25-34, about half in Metro Manila
whatWorked: A3 started 14 message conversations for ₱99. A6 came next with 10.
It also got the most link clicks: 31 for ₱99, against 24 for A6.
The hook named the moment, not the person: "nagluto ako ng 5 ulam pero ang tinanong ng bisita: ano yung mabango? 😭"
whatToPostNext: Show the jar lit on the sala table before guests arrive, next to the guest glasses.
Match a scent to each kind of visit: Pandan Coconut for a handaan, Calamansi Basil for morning coffee.
Keep day 4 for Officemates buying an exchange gift, to see if second place holds.
icp.caveat: Each audience got ₱99 for 3 days, so these are small numbers: 14 conversations against 10. That clears Hunch's bar for a clear lead, but with numbers this small, next week's posts are the real check on whether it holds into December.

notes: Using sample results. No real ads were run.
Elle is a persona made for this demo.

verdict.explanation: Noche Buena hosts won: A3 started 14 message conversations for ₱99. Officemates buying an exchange gift came second with 10. Next week, aim six posts at hosting at home and keep day 4 to test the exchange gift again.

caveatChecks.rule: Spend differs by more than 20% between audiences
